title: Not a free love or desire (book 4, chapter 11)
source_text: LIX. Istam autem delectationem in nullo amore, vel desiderio libero consistere, juxta Doctoris illius principia manifestum est. Quandoquidem etiam ad desiderandum & amandum Deum, & quodlibet verum ac spirituale bonum, libero voluntatis motu, necessaria est: cum desiderium & amor ejusmodi sint actus boni, qui sine suavitatis gratia non possunt a voluntate proficisci. Qua de re pluribus agit Jansenius, libro quarto de gratia Christi salvatoris capite undecimo, cujus titulus est, Delectatio ista coelestis, secundum Augustini mentem, est actus vitalis & indeliberatus animae: & quidem amoris ac desiderii praecedentis consensum, ac delectationem illam, quae & quies animi, & gaudium dicitur.
pass_a_gloss: LIX. But that this delight consists in no free love, or desire, is manifest according to that Doctor's principles. Since it is necessary even for desiring and loving God, and any true and spiritual good, with a free motion of the will: since desire and love of this kind are good acts, which without the grace of sweetness cannot proceed from the will. Of which matter Jansenius treats at more length, in the fourth book on the grace of Christ the saviour chapter eleven, whose title is, This heavenly delight, according to Augustine's mind, is a vital and indeliberate act of the soul: and indeed of love and desire preceding consent, and that delight, which is called both rest of the mind, and joy.
pass_b_english: Thesis LIX. On that doctor's principles it is plain that this delight does not consist in any free love or desire. It is needed even in order to desire and love God, or any true spiritual good, by a free movement of the will, since such desire and love are good acts, which cannot come from the will without the grace of sweetness.

Jansenius deals with this more fully in De gratia Christi Salvatoris, book 4, chapter 11, whose heading is: 'This heavenly delight, in Augustine's mind, is a vital and indeliberate act of the soul; that is, an act of the love and desire that come before consent and before the delight that is also called the mind's rest and joy.'

lemmas.latin: in nullo amore, vel desiderio libero consistere
lemmas.gloss: consists in no free love, or desire
is a vital and indeliberate act of the soul

choices.why: An act arising before the mind deliberates (LVII), as opposed to a free, deliberate act.

bible_refs: Cornelius Jansenius, Augustinus (Louvain, 1640), tome 3, De gratia Christi Salvatoris, book 4.
